title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as far as it can be inferred from this and the neighbouring pages. G is a linear group, apparently GL_2 or SL_2 over a base, possibly a scheme of units E'. PG is its projectivisation. ρ and σ act on G, almost certainly by conjugation, since the next page writes uσ(u)^{-1} as a commutator [u,σ]. The previous page shows that Tr σ = 0 is equivalent to σ^2 being scalar. So σ is a lift of an involution of PG, and the situation looks like lifting relations from PSL_2/PGL_2 to SL_2/GL_2, where a sign ambiguity ε ∈ μ_2 appears. This reading is plausible but not certain.

Equation (2) defines G*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G×G×E'×E', the scheme of solutions (α,β,μ,ε). Its image in PG×PG×E' is the solution scheme G*~_{ρ,σ} of the projectivised equation (1). Projecting onto the last factor gives ε : G*_{ρ,σ} → μ_2.

(11) Grothendieck notes, with an exclamation mark, that ε factors through G*~_{ρ,σ}. Because σ^2 is scalar, the sign ε is already determined by the projective data (α,β,μ) mod scalars. So ε is an invariant of the projective solution.

(12) The 'unsigned' solution scheme G_{ρ,σ} is the fibre ε^{-1}(1) inside G*_{ρ,σ}.

(13) Analogously, G~_{ρ,σ} := ε~^{-1}(1) ⊂ G*~_{ρ,σ}. Then G_{ρ,σ} is the inverse image of G~_{ρ,σ} in G×G×E'.

(14) There is a morphism G*_{ρ,σ} → X_{ρ,σ} × μ_2, given by (α,β,μ,ε) ↦ ((ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = εβσ(β)^{-1}, μ), ε). Here X_{ρ,σ} is a scheme of 'twisted commutator' data. The fibre over a section ((ξ,η,μ),ε) is the scheme of solutions (α,β) of (15a) αρ(α)^{-1} = ξ and (15b) βσ(β)^{-1} = εη. These are Lang/twisted-conjugacy type equations, so each fibre is a torsor-like scheme.

The next page resolves this. It uses a privileged solution α = u, characterised as a section of B'_0. It then seeks β = uτ with τσ(τ)^{-1} = ε, which reduces the sign problem to a single equation.

Purpose: to describe the solution schemes of the 'loop equation' (relations among generators of finite order, like ρ and σ in SL_2(Z)/PSL_2(Z)) as fibrations over a parameter scheme. This is part of the 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' following the Longue Marche, with careful tracking of the central μ_2 when passing between G and PG.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The factorisation of ε through the projective solution scheme is asserted, not proved here; it depends on the scalarity of σ^2 established on the previous page.

The notation fluctuates: the transcription has G*~ versus G̃*, and E' versus 𝔼'. The arrow in (14) is written G_{ρ,σ}^{*} with the * crossed out, although the map naturally needs ε, i.e. it lives on G*.

ideas.what: A sign invariant ε ∈ μ_2 of solutions of a group-theoretic equation, which descends from G to PG and splits the solution scheme into the fibres ε = ±1
ideas.modern_name: obstruction / sign class for lifting along the central extension μ_2 → SL_2 → PSL_2 (or GL_2 → PGL_2)

ideas.what: Fibring the solution scheme over the values of the twisted-conjugacy maps α ↦ αρ(α)^{-1}, β ↦ βσ(β)^{-1}; the fibres are solution schemes of Lang-type equations
ideas.modern_name: Lang map / twisted conjugacy; torsors under centralisers

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping inside a longer computation: a sign ε ∈ μ_2 descends to the projective solution scheme, and the solution scheme is fibred over twisted-commutator data. It is of local interest for the 'équation des lacets' manuscript but contains no new result or connection on its own.
transcription_corrections: The first line reads 'qui se factorise d'ailleurs par G*~_{ρ,σ} :', and (11) is ε~ : G*~_{ρ,σ} → μ_2.
The inclusion G_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G*_{ρ,σ} carries a crossed-out label '(11)'.
Under the brace in (14) it reads '∈ Γ X_{ρ,σ}'. Under ε it reads '∈ Γμ_2', written vertically as an ∈ symbol above Γμ_2.
The text reads 'l'image inverse dans G×G×E' de G̃_{ρ,σ}'.
